NimbusWorks Inc. — Travel & Expense Policy
Document ID: FIN-POL-003
Last Updated: April 2026

1. General Principles
All business expenses must be reasonable, necessary, and directly related to company business. Employees should book the most cost-effective option available that meets business needs. Personal expenses must never be submitted, even accidentally mixed with business expenses.

2. Expense Submission
All expenses must be submitted via the Expensify portal within 30 days of being incurred. Each expense requires an itemized receipt for amounts over $25. Expenses submitted more than 60 days after the transaction date will not be reimbursed except with VP-level approval.

3. Travel Booking
Flights should be booked at least 14 days in advance when possible, in economy class for flights under 6 hours. Flights over 6 hours may be booked in premium economy. Hotel bookings should not exceed $250/night in major cities ($180/night elsewhere) without prior approval.

4. Meals
Daily meal reimbursement while traveling is capped at $75/day ($20 breakfast, $25 lunch, $30 dinner). Client meals are reimbursable at reasonable cost but require the client's name and company to be noted in the expense report. Alcohol is reimbursable only for client entertainment, up to $50 per event, and requires manager approval.

5. Ground Transportation
Rideshare and taxi expenses are reimbursable for business travel. Mileage for personal vehicle use is reimbursed at the current IRS standard mileage rate. Parking and tolls are reimbursable with receipts.

6. Approval Thresholds
Expenses under $500 require manager approval only. Expenses between $500 and $2,000 require manager and department head approval. Expenses over $2,000 require VP approval and must be pre-approved before the expense is incurred.

7. Non-Reimbursable Items
The company does not reimburse: personal entertainment, traffic or parking fines, airline seat upgrades beyond premium economy, spa or gym services, or lost personal property.

NimbusWorks Inc. — Employee Leave Policy
Document ID: HR-POL-002
Last Updated: March 2026

1. Annual Leave
All full-time employees accrue 18 days of paid annual leave per calendar year, credited at 1.5 days per completed month of service. Annual leave must be requested at least 5 working days in advance through the HR portal, except in emergencies. Unused annual leave can be carried over into the next year up to a maximum of 10 days; anything beyond that is forfeited unless approved by a department head.

2. Sick Leave
Employees are entitled to 12 days of paid sick leave per year. A medical certificate is required for any sick leave exceeding 2 consecutive days. Sick leave does not carry over and resets on January 1st each year.

3. Parental Leave
Primary caregivers are entitled to 16 weeks of paid parental leave. Secondary caregivers are entitled to 4 weeks of paid leave. Parental leave requests should be submitted at least 30 days before the expected start date, along with supporting documentation (e.g., medical certificate or adoption papers).

4. Bereavement Leave
Employees may take up to 5 paid days of bereavement leave for the death of an immediate family member (spouse, child, parent, or sibling), and up to 2 days for extended family. No advance notice is required; employees should inform their manager and HR as soon as possible.

5. Unpaid Leave
Employees with at least 1 year of tenure may request unpaid leave of up to 30 days for personal reasons, subject to manager and HR approval. Requests must be submitted at least 2 weeks in advance.

6. Public Holidays
NimbusWorks observes 12 public holidays per year, as published annually on the HR portal. If a public holiday falls on a weekend, the following Monday is observed as a holiday instead.

7. Leave Approval Process
All leave requests are submitted via the HR portal and require approval from the employee's direct manager. Leave exceeding 10 consecutive days additionally requires HR sign-off. Managers must respond to leave requests within 3 business days.

NimbusWorks Inc. — Information Security Policy
Document ID: IT-SEC-014
Last Updated: January 2026

1. Password Requirements
All employee accounts must use passwords of at least 14 characters, including a mix of uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols. Passwords must be changed every 180 days. Password reuse across the last 8 passwords is prohibited. Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is mandatory for all accounts with access to production systems, email, or the VPN.

2. Device Policy
Company laptops must have full-disk encryption enabled and automatic screen lock after 5 minutes of inactivity. Personal devices used for work (BYOD) must be enrolled in the company's Mobile Device Management (MDM) system before accessing company email or Slack.

3. Data Classification
Data is classified into three tiers:
- Public: may be shared externally without restriction.
- Internal: for employee use only, not to be shared outside the company.
- Confidential: includes customer data, financial records, and source code. Requires encryption at rest and in transit, and access is logged and reviewed quarterly.

4. Incident Reporting
Any suspected security incident (phishing email, lost device, unauthorized access, malware) must be reported to security@nimbusworks.example within 1 hour of discovery. Do not attempt to investigate or remediate the incident yourself — forward suspicious emails to the security team without opening attachments or links.

5. Remote Access
All remote access to internal systems must go through the company VPN. Split-tunneling is disabled by default. VPN sessions automatically time out after 8 hours of inactivity.

6. Third-Party Tools
Employees must not install or connect third-party SaaS tools (including AI tools, browser extensions, and automation platforms like Zapier, Make, or n8n) to company systems without approval from the IT Security team via the Tool Request Form. Any tool that will process Confidential data requires a Data Processing Assessment before approval.

7. Security Training
All employees must complete annual security awareness training within 30 days of their hire anniversary. Failure to complete training may result in suspension of system access.

NimbusWorks Inc. — New Employee Onboarding Guide
Document ID: HR-ONB-007
Last Updated: February 2026

1. Before Your First Day
IT will ship your laptop to arrive 2 business days before your start date. You will receive a welcome email with your company email address and instructions to set up MFA. Please complete the pre-boarding paperwork (tax forms, direct deposit, emergency contacts) in the HR portal before day one.

2. Your First Day
Arrive at the office by 9:30 AM (or join the virtual welcome session if remote). You'll meet your onboarding buddy, get a facilities tour, and complete a laptop setup session with IT. Your manager will walk you through your 30/60/90-day plan.

3. First Week Checklist
- Complete mandatory security awareness training (see IT-SEC-014).
- Set up your accounts: email, Slack, Google Workspace, and the HR portal.
- Meet with your manager for a 1:1 to review goals and expectations.
- Join your team's standing meetings (calendar invites are sent by your manager).
- Review the Employee Leave Policy (HR-POL-002) and Expense Policy (FIN-POL-003).

4. Probation Period
All new hires undergo a 90-day probation period. A formal check-in occurs at day 30, day 60, and day 90 with your manager and an HR representative. Full benefits (including the 401k match) begin after successful completion of probation.

5. Equipment & Access
Standard equipment includes a laptop, monitor, and headset. Additional equipment requests go through the IT Request Form. Access to internal tools (GitHub, AWS, Notion, etc.) is provisioned based on your role and requires manager approval, typically completed within 2 business days.

6. Who to Contact
- IT support: it-help@nimbusworks.example
- HR questions: hr@nimbusworks.example
- Payroll: payroll@nimbusworks.example
- Security incidents: security@nimbusworks.example

7. Buddy Program
Every new hire is paired with an onboarding buddy from a different team for their first 60 days. The buddy is a resource for informal questions — process, culture, "who do I ask about X" — separate from your manager.

NimbusWorks Inc. — Remote & Hybrid Work Policy
Document ID: HR-POL-009
Last Updated: May 2026

1. Work Arrangements
NimbusWorks operates a hybrid model by default: employees are expected in the office at least 2 days per week (Tuesday and Thursday are the core in-office days for most teams). Fully remote arrangements require director-level approval and are evaluated on a role-by-role basis.

2. Core Hours
All employees, regardless of location, are expected to be online and reachable between 11:00 AM and 4:00 PM in their local time zone. Outside of core hours, employees may set their own schedule as long as deliverables are met.

3. Home Office Stipend
Remote and hybrid employees receive a one-time $500 home office setup stipend in their first 90 days, plus an ongoing $40/month stipend for internet and utilities. Requests are submitted through the Expensify portal under the "Home Office" category.

4. Working From Abroad
Employees may work from a foreign country for up to 20 business days per year without special approval, provided they notify HR at least 2 weeks in advance for tax and compliance tracking. Longer arrangements require legal and HR review due to tax and visa implications.

5. Equipment for Remote Work
Company laptops, monitors, and headsets ship to the employee's registered home address. Employees are responsible for a secure home network (WPA2/WPA3 encrypted Wi-Fi) and must use the company VPN when accessing internal systems, per the Information Security Policy (IT-SEC-014).

6. Meeting Etiquette
Cameras should be on for team meetings unless there is a stated accommodation. Meetings with any remote participant must have a virtual join option — no "phone in the corner of the room" setups.

7. Performance Expectations
Remote and hybrid employees are held to the same performance standards as in-office employees. Managers are expected to evaluate output and outcomes rather than hours logged or visible activity.
